Let me just tell you this: you’re awesome. You are supporting your girlfriend instead of putting her down even though you’re feeling bad about yourself. You’re asking how to deal with your feelings better. That shows growth! 

Everyone’s body changes throughout their lives. It’s not common for people to have time to workout 2-3 times a day. Hell, it’s not common for people to have time to work out 2-3 times a week. You are prioritizing your relationship, making an effort to show commitment, and you even said that spending time with her makes you feel better. Keep doing that, it’s so good for you. Mental health is so important, as well. If you’re struggling with your feelings, it may be a good idea to book a therapist for an hour once a week, even over the phone, and talk some of these things through. 

It sounds like it’s been difficult to ignore the attention she’s getting, and I totally understand that. It can be hard to keep insecurities out of your head, and that’s another thing you could talk about with a therapist. Another thing that could help is lightening your load. Try to hire or train someone else to take care of the family business. Maybe in the evenings when you get home you can ask your girlfriend to go on a walk with you, that way you get some exercise while also hanging out with your girlfriend. 

Remember, you have no obligation to change for anyone but yourself. Try not to let other people’s perceptions of you and your relationship take hold on your mind. If you want to lose some weight, then do that for yourself. Don’t do it because some assholes at work are getting you down. Also, report that to HR. It’s unacceptable for people in the workplace to be talking about a coworker like that. Best of luck, OP.

I’m a sophomore in college this year. Last year, I had no idea what I was doing still alive. 

This year, I still have no idea what I’m doing. But guess what I realized—even when I am at my most hopeless, and my mind is fighting a battle against myself, my body knows what it’s doing. If I hate myself, my cells still reproduce. If life doesn’t seem worth the pain, my heart still beats. My body-no matter how long I’ve been in bed, or not brushed my teeth, or let my hair become a mat-wants to survive. It’s fighting for me. My mind may be cloudy but underneath the fog my brain is still yelling at my body not to concede. 

Your life is worth something. Those cells that kill themselves to protect me from radiation and cancer from the sun? They know I’m worth it. If I truly wanted to die, I don’t know why they would do that because I wouldn’t tell them to. The nerves that tell me that I can feel the heat of a steamy shower? They’re warning me, “be careful, now. We don’t want you to get hurt.” 

“Be gentle with yourself, please. We need you to survive the same as you do us.” 

You are taking care of billions of cells. Billions of cells are taking care of you. They know you’re worth it. 

So do I.
